title: TikTok Discovered a Blind, Pale, Worm-Like Fish
gist: A previously undescribed blind cavefish species was first spotted in a 2024 TikTok video from a borewell near the India-Nepal border, prompting Thackeray Wildlife Foundation researchers to track it down after a difficult search.

themes.theme: Social media as a species-discovery channel

insights.claim: A previously unknown species of blind cavefish was discovered by scientists only after being captured in a 2024 TikTok video showing it emerging from a borewell near the India-Nepal border.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Illustrates social media as an emerging, informal discovery channel for previously undocumented species, a notable trend for citizen-science and biodiversity monitoring.
insights.quote: A previously unknown (to scientists) species of blind cavefish that was recently discovered after being caught on TikTok.

insights.claim: By some estimates, nearly 90 percent of life on Earth has not yet been formally described by science, out of millions of undiscovered species.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A frequently-cited biodiversity statistic underscoring the scale of undocumented species diversity.
insights.quote: by some estimates, nearly 90 percent of life on our planet hasn't been formally described by science

insights.claim: Researchers from the Thackeray Wildlife Foundation, led by Akshay Khandekar, struggled to locate and sample the newly discovered cavefish species, requiring permission from private borewell and well owners and manual water pumping to find specimens.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Documents the practical field-research difficulty in confirming species identified via informal social media sightings.
insights.quote: Procuring samples of this unusual fish was challenging...Identifying potential handpumps (borewells) and wells, and obtaining permission from their owners to extract water for the purpose of searching for the fish proved difficult.
